title: Adaptive SLA-aware quantization sweep harness (FP16 / INT8 / INT4)
creator: Ava Patel
description: Build a reusable benchmarking and load-testing harness that runs systematic quantization profile sweeps (FP16, INT8, INT4) across representative workloads and automatically evaluates quality vs. performance trade-offs under explicit SLA constraints. The harness should be able to: 1) run parallel experiments to measure tokens/sec and p95 latency under controlled load patterns, 2) compute quality regressions using prompt sets and embedding/LM-based metrics, 3) pick an operational configuration (quant+batching+kernel selection) that meets a target latency SLO while maximizing throughput, and 4) emit regression alerts and create rollback candidates when quality drops exceed thresholds.
acceptance_criteria: Runnable harness that executes FP16/INT8/INT4 sweeps on a per-model basis and produces standardized CSV/JSON results for tokens/sec, p95, median latency, and cost-estimated tokens/unit.
Quality evaluation pipeline integrated: supports exact-match, ROUGE, and embedding-cosine similarity checks against a configurable prompt set.
Adaptive policy module that can select configurations satisfying a declared latency SLO (e.g., p95 <= 120ms) and report expected throughput gain compared to baseline.

Regression detection: automated alert when quality drops > configurable threshold (default: 2% relative for embedding similarity or 1.5 points ROUGE), with a generated rollback candidate and links to failing prompts.
End-to-end tests validating harness on at least two model families (autoregressive and chat-completion style), and on both NVidia A100 and H100 GPU pools in staging.
Integration with Console perf dashboard so each sweep produces a dashboard tile and historical comparison.
Documentation and runbook for how to add new prompt sets, thresholds, and target SLOs for customers.
No production-facing changes without feature flag; default is experimental and gated behind quant-sweep-feature flag.
test_plan: 1) Prepare three workload profiles: short-turn chat (avg 40 tokens), long-form generation (avg 512 tokens), and embedding-heavy batching. 2) For each profile and each quant mode (FP16, INT8, INT4) run 3 load levels (light, medium, heavy) using the load generator harness and collect tokens/sec, p50, p95, p99, and error rates. 3) Run the quality evaluation step: feed canonical prompt set (1000 prompts) and compute exact-match/ROUGE and embedding-cosine against FP16 baseline. 4) Feed results into the adaptive policy that simulates SLA targets (e.g., p95=120ms, p95=200ms) and outputs recommended config. 5) Validate regression detection logic by injecting a synthetic perturbation to INT8 kernels (simulated bug) and confirm alert + rollback candidate generation. 6) Publish CSVs and JSON summaries to internal bucket and create perf dashboard tiles.
initial_results_summary: Initial staging run on model rdx-small-v1 (seq=512) on A100: FP16 baseline tokens/sec=1,220, p95=135ms. INT8 configuration with standard binning: tokens/sec=2,050 (+68%), p95=98ms. INT4 aggressive quant: tokens/sec=3,900 (+220%), p95=76ms. Quality: embedding cosine mean vs FP16 -> INT8=0.986, INT4=0.915. ROUGE-L average delta -> INT8=-0.8, INT4=-4.7. Interpretation: INT8 is within acceptable quality bounds for many low-sensitivity workloads while meeting p95 SLO=120ms; INT4 delivers large throughput gains but fails quality thresholds for most tasks. These numbers are from single sweep and need cross-model validation.
blockers: INT4 kernel support flaky on H100 kernels; currently missing stable fused-gemm path for attention. Engineering to coordinate with kernel owners.
Missing curated per-customer high-sensitivity prompt sets — must request from Solutions Eng for enterprise customers used in gating rules.
Console dashboard tile API lacks an endpoint to accept sweep JSON schema; small console PR required before full automation.
Staging cluster quota constraints during parallel sweep runs — need to schedule runway with infra or throttle parallelism.
